statement: The B4 candidate adapter failed controlled evaluation on the frozen 44-clip Pidgin set. It is rejected for promotion and remains candidates-only. This record does not alter the training-run evidence or the MLflow run, both of which remain accurate: the run did complete, and the loss did fall. What the loss did not do is predict inference quality.

evaluation.provenance: EXTERNAL. These figures were produced by a separate evaluation run and reported to this repository; they have NOT yet been independently reproduced by tooling in this repo. scripts/evaluate_candidate.py is being built for that purpose, and this record will be superseded by one carrying reproduced numbers.
why_the_result_is_trusted: the untouched base scored 0.5133, closely matching the previously recorded 0.5257 Pidgin baseline, which validates the evaluator rather than the candidate
two independent adapter passes agreed at approximately 7.19 and 7.22
adapter hash, base revision, audio checksums and eval manifest were verified
no transcripts or private content were printed

root_cause.summary: Training labels retained the start-of-transcript token, so HuggingFace prepended a second one and the model trained one position out of alignment with inference. The guard intended to strip it compared against bos_token_id and could never fire. CONFIRMED defect and the strongest explanation for the collapse; sole-cause proof requires a corrected A/B run.

measured_evidence.note: In Whisper, bos_token IS <|endoftext|>, not <|startoftranscript|>. The comparison is therefore always false and the strip is dead code.

primary_defect.consequence: labels keep [<|startoftranscript|>, <|lang|>, <|transcribe|>, <|notimestamps|>]. HuggingFace then derives decoder_input_ids = shift_tokens_right(labels, decoder_start_token_id=50258), producing a DUPLICATED <|startoftranscript|> and shifting every target one position later than it appears at inference. NOTE: the language, task and no-timestamps tokens are legitimate Whisper training targets and are NOT the defect -- only the retained SOT is erroneous.

corroborating_evidence.observation: candidate median output 52.5 tokens against a base median of 14; maximum 444 against 71
corroborating_evidence.reading: The candidate generates far past the base. Whether EOS was emitted -- the question that distinguishes termination failure from poor quality -- was NOT measured, and the earlier reading of 444 as '444 + 4 prefix = 448' is withdrawn: generate() returns the prompt inside the sequence while max_new_tokens excludes it. The hardened evaluator records eos_emitted, prompt/generated/total tokens and the stop reason so this can be settled by measurement.

A cross-entropy of 22.5 means near-zero probability mass on the targets, consistent with a one-position shift. It is NOT a calibrated finding: no correctly aligned baseline loss has been measured for this 14-language mixture, so 'too high' rests on general expectation rather than on this corpus. The process point is independent of calibration -- an anomalous number appeared at step 0 of every run and was recorded as an open question rather than investigated.

corroborating_evidence.observation: loss fell steadily to 4.00 while inference collapsed
corroborating_evidence.reading: The model successfully learned the misaligned objective. Descent against a wrong target is not evidence of a right one, and the descent gate cannot distinguish the two.

secondary_factors.assessment: Set on model.config, but generation reads generation_config, where the pinned config carries forced_decoder_ids [[1, null], [2, 50360]], begin_suppress_tokens [220, 50257] and 88 suppress_tokens. The training-time intent and the generation-time behaviour were therefore set in two different places. NOT CONFIRMED as contributing to this failure; it is a correctness hazard found while diagnosing and must be settled before the next run.

High for Whisper LoRA, where 1e-4 to 5e-4 is typical. SUSPECTED aggravating factor only. It would amplify a bad objective but does not explain termination failure, and must not be treated as the cause.

secondary_factors.factor: Pidgin trained via LANG_TOKEN mapping to a proxy token
secondary_factors.assessment: UNQUANTIFIED. Pidgin has no Whisper language token; the run mapped it to a proxy. Whether that mapping is sound is a separate open question and cannot be assessed until the label alignment is fixed.

root_cause.what_the_existing_gates_did_not_catch: Every guard in the training path checked provenance, licensing, exclusions, label LENGTH and loss DESCENT. None checked label CONTENT or decoder alignment, and none evaluated generation. A run can satisfy all of them while training on a mis-specified objective.

consequences.artifacts: remain under candidates/; nothing merged, quantized, registered or deployed
consequences.deferred_rows: the 20 rows remain excluded and unclassified; DQ-2026-001 stays draft
consequences.training_evidence: platform/evidence/training-run-23868bab2d84.json is NOT amended. It recorded a completed run accurately and explicitly disclaimed any quality claim.

required_before_retraining: reproduce the base-versus-candidate result with the hardened evaluator and update this record from EXTERNAL to independently reproduced only if hashes and metrics agree
one-batch overfit and generation smoke test confirming EOS is emitted and no output reaches its limit
pin generation configuration in one place
a small lower-learning-rate sweep rather than reusing 1e-3
a speaker- and session-disjoint validation set plus a separate untouched final holdout, which with only two current speakers likely requires new Pidgin speakers
evaluation-coverage audit for all 14 trained languages
content_policy: checksums, hashes and aggregate metrics only; no transcript, speaker, session or content excerpt appears in this file
revision_note: Revision 2 after independent review. The duplicated start-of-transcript token is a CONFIRMED trainer defect, sufficient to invalidate the run and the strongest explanation for the collapse; sole-cause proof requires a corrected controlled A/B run that has not been performed.

corrections.claim: 444 generated + 4 prefix = 448 proves the decoder cap was hit
corrections.why: generate() returns a sequence INCLUDING the decoder prompt while max_new_tokens excludes it, so 444 is equally consistent with 4 prompt + 440 generated. The external evaluator's token accounting is unknown. A cap hit is now defined operationally: EOS absent AND generated tokens reaching max_new_tokens.

corrections.claim: cross-entropy over all four prefix positions trained the model to emit control tokens as content
corrections.why: language, task and no-timestamps ARE legitimate Whisper training targets; the official collator strips only decoder_start_token_id. Only the retained SOT was erroneous.

corrections.claim: a correctly aligned run opens near 1-3; abort above 6
corrections.why: never measured for this 14-language mixture. Hard gates are the label-alignment assertions and finite loss/gradient checks; loss magnitude is a warning until a per-language aligned base-loss distribution is measured.

corrections.claim: mask the prefix with -100 as an alternative fix
corrections.why: without separately constructing decoder_input_ids the shift would propagate masked values into the decoder inputs in place of the language/task prompt.

corrections.claim: generate() returns a sequence INCLUDING the decoder prompt while max_new_tokens excludes it (given as the reason for withdrawing the 444 arithmetic in revision 2)
corrections.why: measured on the pinned stack: WhisperGenerationMixin._postprocess_outputs returns seek_outputs[:, start_idx:] with start_idx = decoder_input_ids.shape[-1], so the default tensor return has the prompt AND EOS sliced off. The generic generate() rule does not apply to Whisper. The 444 arithmetic stays withdrawn because the external evaluator's version and accounting are unknown, not because of the prompt-inclusion claim.

additional_defects_found_by_review.defect: the identical bos_token_id comparison, so `effective` silently equalled `raw` for every row ever measured
Dataset.__getitem__ calls set_prefix_tokens() per row, so the saved processor was pinned to the last sampled language; run 23868bab shipped one stuck at language='yo'
additional_defects_found_by_review.status: fixed 2026-07-31 -- a clean processor is reloaded from the pinned base

eval_set_status.speaker_and_session_overlap: YES -- shares both speakers and sessions
eval_set_status.verdict: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY from 2026-07-31. Usable to study when the failed checkpoints degenerated. Must not select a checkpoint or support promotion, both because it is not speaker-disjoint and because it has now informed the investigation.
